Closes #6237.

Since #6228, `size(f::AbstractField)` passes `indices(f)` to the grid. Fields adapted for a kernel drop their indices (`indices(f) === nothing`), so the size of an adapted operation errored inside GPU kernels, e.g. `argmin` in `global_wind_driven_gyres.jl`. This uses `axes_indices`, as `axes` already does, and adds a regression test.

body:
This PR adds new functionality to generate a balanced partition given an instance of an immersed boundary.

The internal functions are more general, and can take any "weight map" (which is a field on the underlying grid). For the moment, I have just implemented the weight map as being the total count of active cells per x-y column. This can obviously be improved in the future.

Currently I have only implemented two partitioning algorithms, both of which generate a "Generalised Block Distribution". This is essentially a Cartesian topology of the partition but with different sizes. The first algorithm is an approximation that partitions the x and y directions independently, and the second uses an iterative algorithm from this paper: [Manne, F., Sørevik, T. (1996). Partitioning an array onto a mesh of processors](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-62095-8_50)

I am looking into other, more generalised, partitioning algorithms but they will need some generalisation/abstracting of the current way distributed grids work. This PR gets the initial API in which can then be built on top of.

Things to do:
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests

body: With `extend_halos = true` and open boundaries, the split-explicit substeps use `LocalHaloFilling` and the barotropic kernel steps U, V, η into the Connected halo region. The open-boundary halo fills, however, cover only `1:N` in the tangential direction, so those halo rows are left unfilled and the distributed solution diverges from the serial one. This rebuilds the substep fill kernels for distributed `LocalHaloFilling` so the tangential extent of west/east and south/north fills matches the barotropic kernel range in Connected dimensions. The distributed-vs-serial comparisons in `test/mpi/split_explicit_boundaries.jl` that were marked `@test_broken` for this case are now strict and pass (4 CPU ranks). body:
Once again, taken out of #5799.

> A `Field` adapted for a kernel drops its indices, which become
> `nothing`. The axes of a field already read that as `(:, :, :)`, but
> the index intersection of operations indexed into it, so computing the
> indices, axes, or size of an operation on adapted fields threw a
> `MethodError`. GPUArrays 12 reductions run into this both inside the
> kernel, where the reduction indexes through the operation's axes, and
> on the host, where Adapt.jl rebuilds the reshaped operation from its
> size.
title: Treat the dropped indices of adapted fields as the full range

body:
The centered momentum fluxes multiply a cell-center area by an interpolated velocity. Where face areas differ between neighboring faces, as next to `PartialCellBottom` partial cells, the resulting mass fluxes do not satisfy continuity on momentum cells, so centered advection does not conserve kinetic energy. An inviscid `NonhydrostaticModel` with the default `Centered()` over a partial-cell staircase reaches `NaN` within 100 time steps. The fluxes now interpolate the face transports, as the upwind-biased fluxes already do.

- The kinetic energy conservation test now also runs on `PartialCellBottom`, with volume-weighted energy; it fails before this change.

Stacked on #6187.

body:
Yes, also taken out of #5799, I'm done for this morning 🥲 

> A `ConditionalOperation` that applies a function took the element type
> of its operand, so `any(isnan, field)` claimed floating-point elements
> while producing `Bool`s. GPUArrays 12 reductions derive their
> accumulator from the element type and rejected `any` and `all`, since
> `|` and `&` of floats always throw. The element type now follows the
> function, and the mask a reduction substitutes where a condition
> doesn't hold, e.g. in immersed cells, is converted to the type of the
> function's values rather than of the field's. Infinite masks, the
> neutral elements of `maximum` and `minimum`, become the extreme values
> of integer and `Bool` types instead of failing to convert.
title: Give conditional operations the type of their function's values
